answer: YES, all 16. Every node the walk failed holds a `recordRetirement` row with `status: retired` and `verdict: absent-verified`, written 2026-09-17T09:57:38Z-09:58:02Z -- about 30 minutes BEFORE the walk ran (2026-09-17T10:28:02Z). The walk nevertheless graded all 16 `BP-MEANING-01` with `reason: HTTP 404` and recorded `declinedRetirement.accepted: 0, storeErrors: 0`, because main's predicate admits only the `not_baked` token, so the serve's `record_retired` body is never recognised as the declared refusal and the store half is never reached.
whyThisMatters: It closes the loop for the integration seat's re-walk of this exact run (`eb1d2676-df0c-4432-afb8-629d5808d6a1`): half (ii) is already satisfied for the whole cohort at the walk's own timestamp, so the only thing that was failing these rows was half (i) -- the token P-301 adds. A re-walk of the same run with this branch is therefore expected to read 16/16 RECORD_RETIRED, 0 BP-MEANING-01, walk verdict pass -- and that expectation is falsifiable by running it rather than asserted here.
notThisLanesToGrade: The re-walk is the integration seat's, per the dispatch. This artifact is a read-only measurement, not a verdict.
